text:
anya: Heads-up — INT8 KV landed on staging this morning. Running downstream smoke tests and seeing small but consistent decode quality blips on long contexts + a 10–20% P95 tail latency bump. filing here to coordinate. :eyes:
kevin: saw the same on canary around 09:12 PT, started a quick profile. looks like KV memcpy patterns changed.
sam: dropping raw flamegraphs in case useful. short summary: CPU side memcpy spikes during decode step when KV size > 1.5GB.
perf-bot: summary: run_id=run_1772345, model=redwood-v2-small, mode=INT8-KV, avg_lat=82ms, p95_lat=210ms (+18%), kv_mem=1.6GB (was 2.1GB in FP8). quality_delta=BLEU -0.6, exact-match -0.4
anya: thanks — can you paste the exact perf cmd you used? I want to reproduce locally and compare INT8 vs FP8 KV flows.
kevin: sure —

```
./perf_decode --model redwood-v2-small --kv-quant INT8 --batch 1 --ctx 4096 --profile /tmp/run_1772345
```
copy of `perf_trace.txt` attached to the thread (uploaded).
maria: quick note: allocator switch in the kernel selector landed last week (PR #2431). It can change how KV buffers are aligned which might affect memcpy thresholds. might be related.
sam: i repro'd locally. INT8 KV reduces memory but triggers a fallback memcpy path in the decoder's gather kernel for sequences > 2048 because alignment assumptions don't hold. that extra memcpy plus a cache-miss pattern explains tail latency.
anya: oh — so it's not purely compute, it's movement + alignment. do we have a microbenchmark that isolates the gather path?
kevin: yes. added a tiny bench:
```
bench_gather --kv-format=int8 --seq-len=4096 --iters=1000
# results: mean=0.34ms, p95=1.2ms (int8)
bench_gather --kv-format=fp8 --seq-len=4096 --iters=1000
# results: mean=0.28ms, p95=0.9ms (fp8)
```
small but consistent gap.
perf-bot: node-level profile attached: top sources: memcpy (22%), gather_kernel (18%), token_decode (15%).
maria: hypothesis: INT8 packing reduces value size but misaligns rows for our vectorized gather (requires 16-byte lanes). the runtime picks a generic kernel when misaligned.
anya: can we change kernel selection heuristic to prefer an aligned copy that does an in-place reformat once at load time (amortize cost) instead of per-decode memcpy?
sam: proto patch: when loading KV pages, if format==INT8 and rows % 16 != 0 then preformat into aligned buffer on load. tested on staging: memory +0.1GB but p95 tail latency returned to baseline. quality unchanged.
kevin: that's promising. what's the cost for Dedicated workload where KV sizes are 10s of GB? will extra copy bump hot start time?
maria: yes, startup copy cost will increase. propose heuristic: preformat if total_kv < 4GB (interactive) else do on-demand reformat for large KV with background async worker.
anya: agreed. can you open a perf experiment? two arms: (A) preformat-on-load for <4GB, (B) async background reformat + streaming decode fallback. measure cold-start, p95, mem.
kevin: will set up AB test on staging. experiment id: kv-quant-reformat-177. will run 8 hours.
perf-bot: experiment started: id=kv-quant-reformat-177, variants=A/B, samples=0/0. will post interim stats.
anya: also can we add a quick regression check to CI: if kv-format changes from FP8->INT8, run a small decode sweep for long contexts (2k,4k) and assert p95 delta < 25% and bleu delta < 1.0?
maria: i can add that gate. will PR tonight.
sam: one more datapoint: decode quality blip seems to correlate with aggressive calibration window we used when converting KV to INT8. ran calib with longer history and quality returned to baseline, albeit with slightly worse memory.
anya: ok — two levers: alignment preformat and calibration window. parallel tasks: kevin runs perf AB, sam experiments with calibration params + posts numbers, maria adds CI gate + kernel heuristic PR. I'll track in the runtime board. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
